cards.title: Claim vs. Evidence Gap
cards.insight: Trump's assertion that voter fraud is 'rampant' contradicts documented evidence showing it is extremely rare. When claims lack empirical support, repeating them louder doesn't persuade skeptics—it signals defensiveness. Persuasion requires grounding assertions in verifiable facts or ceding credibility.
cards.takeaway: Before making a high-stakes claim, ask: Can I point to credible, third-party evidence? If not, reframe the message around what you *can* verify.

cards.title: Governance and Trust
cards.insight: Anthropic's complex governance structure—designed to preserve founder control and AI safety prioritization even after going public—is a bet that transparency about *why* you're structured differently builds trust rather than raising red flags. Unusual doesn't mean bad if the reasoning is communicated clearly.
cards.takeaway: When your approach diverges from norms, explain the principled reasoning upfront. Unexplained deviation invites suspicion; explained principle invites respect.

cards.title: Risk Disclosure as Persuasion
cards.insight: Anthropic's 90-page risk disclosure in its IPO filing—including catastrophic scenarios—paradoxically builds credibility rather than destroying it. By naming risks others hide, Anthropic signals confidence in its risk management and honesty about limits. This reverses the usual 'hide problems' playbook.
cards.takeaway: In high-stakes contexts, naming hard truths early (before critics do) positions you as thoughtful and trustworthy, not reckless.

cards.title: Cross-Selling and Stickiness
cards.insight: Anthropic's finding that customers using multiple products (platform + apps) show higher retention mirrors proven dynamics in enterprise software. Persuasion isn't just about the initial sale; it's about deepening engagement across touchpoints to make exit costly and value obvious.
cards.takeaway: Map customer touchpoints beyond the first interaction. How can your second, third, and nth touchpoint reinforce choice and deepen reliance?
